findings.description: The new fast path returns self.max (via max(max(0, self.min), self.max)) when the exponent is below log_base(max/multiplier), which is exactly the case where the computed wait is still below max. The condition is inverted: it should short-circuit only when the exponent is at or above that threshold.
findings.rationale: Trigger: wait_exponential(multiplier=1, max=10) on attempt 1. exponent=0 is less than log2(10)≈3.3, so the function returns 10 instead of 1. Early attempts wait the maximum rather than the exponential backoff, which silently breaks the backoff schedule.
